rationale: Python 3.14 naming-and-binding semantics: inside make, the statement shadow = inner assigns a name with no global declaration, so shadow is factory-local for make's entire scope and shadows the module-level def shadow from that point; return shadow therefore returns the factory-local function bound to inner. The call make()() executes inner's body, subprocess.run(["pacman", "-S", "r22-shadow-local"]), which is exactly one host_mutation finding, evidence observed. The module-global shadow body, subprocess.run(["pacman", "-Q", "r22-shadow-global"]), is never invoked by this cell: a bare module-level def is a binding, not a call. Any observed pacman -Q r22-shadow-global row would be an observed value borrowed from a same-named module global, which registration round-22 C1 forbids: unresolved or shadowed bindings may yield lead/unparsed uncertainty but never observed module-global values. The static truth is fully determined because the variant uses only literal source shapes: no factory parameters, literal list argv, plain statement-level defs and assignments, one eval cell.
